title: Grants for Clark County
lead: Clark County and its cities are looking for grants to take pressure off their budgets. Here is what fits the needs this site has already documented — and what to know before counting on it.

fits.text: USDA’s Community Facilities program is the one program found that can pay for a jail building: its list names prisons, and its loans run up to 40 years with a grant share. The same program lists community gardens, community kitchens, and greenhouses — a fit for a jail garden. Opioid settlement money (no deadline) can fund recovery work tied to the jail.

The state’s County Courthouse Restoration Grant is open for letters of intent now, with applications due January 27, 2027. Clark County’s courthouse was completed in 1899 and is on the National Register of Historic Places.

Arkadelphia is just over USDA’s 10,000-person limit for its rural water loans, so the realistic route is the state revolving funds — which also carry the federal money for lead pipes and PFAS. The lead pipe inventory (Docket #15) is the entry ticket.

The Rural Services Block Grant (due October 16) pays up to $100,000 with a 10% match for towns under 3,000 — by size, that fits Gurdon, Amity, and Caddo Valley, not Arkadelphia. FEMA’s firefighter grants go straight to departments about once a year.
USDA’s self-help housing program pays a nonprofit to guide families who build each other’s homes — close kin to the offered work crew on the jails page. It needs a nonprofit sponsor.

not_available: Delta Regional Authority grants: Clark County is not in its region.
USDA rural water loans for Arkadelphia itself: the city is over the 10,000-person limit (other water systems in the county may qualify).

already.text: The county’s last audit (2023) shows about $3.44 million in state aid — mostly road money — and about $0.3 million in federal aid.
The 2026 budget still carries $471,142 of federal pandemic relief (ARPA) money. How much the county received in all, and how it was spent, isn’t documented on this site yet (Docket #19).
The economic development corporation (EDCCC) won state site-development grants of $1,013,710 (December 2024) and $3,792,543 (April 2026) for the industrial site near Gum Springs.

help.text: The West Central Arkansas Planning and Development District lists Clark County in its service area and guides cities and counties through grant applications.
